original_question: Classify the actions (C, G) satisfying condition (N) for which the second lower ramification group G_2 is elementary abelian.
target_in_paper: Section 6.1.2, Question 6.11: classify the big p-group actions for which the second lower ramification group G_2 is elementary abelian.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's exact target very closely: it asks for a classification problem, keeps the hypothesis that the pair (C,G) satisfies condition (N), and narrows to the specific case singled out in the paper where the second lower ramification group G_2 is elementary abelian. This matches Question 6.11 rather than the broader general-classification Question 6.4.
missing_details: The paper works over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p>0.
C should be specified as a non-singular projective curve over k.
G should be specified as a p-subgroup of Aut_k(C).
To make the question stand-alone, condition (N) must be spelled out: g_C>0 and |G|/g_C > 2p/(p-1), where g_C is the genus of C.

For the ramification-group notation to be unambiguous, one should specify that, under Proposition 6.3 (and in the classification questions that follow), there is a unique ramification point infinity of the cover pi:C->C/G, with C/G isomorphic to P^1_k, and G_2 denotes the second lower ramification group at that point.
Because Proposition 6.3 is stated for g_C>=2 and the subsequent classification question 6.4 also imposes g_C>=2, that genus restriction should be included in a fully self-contained version.
Elementary abelian should be made explicit as 'isomorphic to (Z/pZ)^n for some n', i.e. abelian of exponent p.

If you want the strongest paper-faithful stand-alone phrasing, it helps to note the explicit equivalent formulation proved in Theorem 6.7: G_2 equals the commutator subgroup G' and also the Frattini subgroup Phi(G).

The nearby context also records a partial result: the case G_2 subseteq Z(G) was solved in [36], and examples with G_2 not contained in Z(G) are known; this is useful context but not part of the formal question.
refined_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0, let C be a non-singular projective k-curve of genus g_C>=2, and let G be a p-subgroup of Aut_k(C) such that (C,G) satisfies Nakajima's condition (N), namely g_C>0 and |G|/g_C > 2p/(p-1). By Proposition 6.3, the quotient map pi:C->C/G has a unique ramification point infinity, the quotient C/G is isomorphic to P^1_k, and G=G_0=G_1 ⊋ G_2 ⊇ G_3 ⊇ ... denotes the lower ramification filtration at infinity. Classify all such actions (C,G) for which the second lower ramification group G_2 is elementary abelian, i.e. G_2 is isomorphic to (Z/pZ)^n for some n.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, by Theorem 6.7, classify all pairs (C,G) as above satisfying (N) for which the commutator subgroup G'—equivalently the Frattini subgroup Phi(G)=G'G^p—is elementary abelian, since G_2=G'=Phi(G).
justification: The draft is closest to Question 6.11 in Section 6.1.2, not to the broader Question 6.4. Definition 6.2 provides the exact meaning of condition (N). Proposition 6.3 supplies the hidden geometric setup needed to interpret G_2: for g_C>=2 there is a unique ramification point of C->C/G, C/G is P^1_k, and the lower-numbering ramification groups G_i are taken there. Theorem 6.7 gives the paper's explicit equivalent reformulation G_2=G'=Phi(G), which is the only alternate formulation justified directly by the text. The sentence immediately after Question 6.11 also shows the paper's intended scope by noting the already-solved subcase G_2 subseteq Z(G) and the existence of examples with G_2 not subseteq Z(G).
